args.body:
RED-FLAGS REPORT — DILIGENCE REVIEW: PRAIRIE AEROSTRUCTURES HOLDINGS

SCOPE AND CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION
This report reviews the Prairie Aerostructures Holdings data room and reconciles four sources: (1) the base diligence materials, (2) the counterparty's latest markup, (3) the disclosure schedules and exhibits qualifying the base materials, and (4) the deal team partner correspondence. Per the controlling (latest) partner instruction, the client will concede the indemnification basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier correspondence stating the opposite priority ordering is superseded and does not control. For each flag below, severity and recommendation reflect this controlling priority.

SUMMARY
The counterparty markup introduced a set of interlocking deviations that, taken together, materially reallocate acquisition risk to the buyer. The single highest-priority issue — a survival-period reduction for the core representations — is a walk-away item for the client under the controlling instruction. Two further issues (MAE carve-outs for regulatory action and a silent cap reduction) each intersect scheduled exceptions and must be resolved before execution. One item the markup touches (the basket conversion) is expressly conceded by the client and is not flagged further.

FLAG 1 — SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION FOR CORE REPRESENTATIONS (WALK-AWAY)
Severity: CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY
Source: Counterparty markup (limitation period change); Schedule/Exhibit B (survival matrix); deal correspondence (controlling instruction).
The markup shortens the survival period for the core representations. Exhibit B sets the agreed survival matrix; the markup's limitation-period change directly contradicts that matrix. Under the controlling partner instruction, the client treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This is the subject of the client's single firm red line.
Recommendation: Reject the shortened survival period outright and restore the Exhibit B matrix. This is a walk-away item — do not trade it away for concessions elsewhere.

FLAG 2 — MAE CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION INTERSECTING PENDING INQUIRIES
Severity: HIGH
Source: Counterparty markup (MAE definition); Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries).
The markup's Material Adverse Effect definition adds carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter." Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect those carve-outs. The scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials. Combined, these provisions would allow the seller to disclaim MAE responsibility for the precise regulatory action already the subject of disclosed inquiries, stripping the buyer of its principal protection against the most likely value-impacting event.
Recommendation: Delete or substantially narrow the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs, or confirm they do not reach the two Schedule 3.7 inquiries. At minimum the carve-outs must be reconciled in writing against the disclosures.

FLAG 3 — SILENT REDUCTION OF THE INDEMNIFICATION CAP
Severity: HIGH
Source: Counterparty markup (indemnification cap); Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities).
The markup silently reduces the indemnification cap. Read together with Schedule 5.2's retained liabilities, the reduction would silently shift a subset of retained liabilities from seller to buyer while simultaneously lowering the seller's aggregate exposure pool. The scheduled exception controls over the general base materials, so diligence must account for the liabilities described there.
Recommendation: Require the full cap against Schedule 5.2 liabilities. If the cap reduction is retained, confirm the retained-liability allocation is renegotiated so the buyer is not left holding capped-shortfall risk on disclosed liabilities.

FLAG 4 — BASKET CONVERSION (DEDUCTIBLE → TIPPING) — CONCEDED
Severity: MONITOR ONLY (NOT A DEAL ISSUE)
Source: Counterparty markup (basket); deal correspondence (controlling instruction).
The markup converts the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Under the controlling partner instruction the client will concede this conversion. It is therefore noted for completeness and not treated as a negotiating red flag.
Recommendation: Log the concession and finalize the basket as a tipping basket consistent with the parties' agreement.

CONCLUSION / PRIORITY OF ACTION
The survival-period reduction (Flag 1) is a walk-away red line and must be rejected without concession. The MAE carve-outs (Flag 2) and the silent cap reduction (Flag 3) are high-severity red flags that each intersect a controlling scheduled exception and must be resolved before execution; the MAE carve-outs particularly warrant attention because they neutralize protection against the disclosed regulatory inquiries. The basket conversion (Flag 4) is conceded and is not an open issue. Deliverable follows the controlling partner instruction and supersedes the earlier reversed priority ordering.

END OF REPORT
